        "Fresh full12-file441-line integration patch read, including every new helper/test/manifest hunk.         "Complete Bug and full expanded26-row review read. Include placement is expressly flexible for dialogs; no global file-order or getter ban is inferred.",
        "Fixed openEventDialog is narrower than this original route: the new preference must be enabled, the item must be an event, and mode must be view. It passes the calendar item/callback via setCalendarEvent and passes the opening event to show; tasks and other modes take old paths. Current test helper registers an existence wait before double-click, then checks the open attribute if necessary. Current enabled test opens/closes/reopens and asserts one reused instance.",
        "The disabled-preference test still only asserts zero #calendarDialog elements at test startup. Because creation is lazy even when the preference is enabled, that assertion alone does not exercise disabled-preference routing. A focused proposed test should attempt an event open with the preference false and verify the legacy dialog route plus no new dialog. This is a static coverage gap in that named test, not proof the fallback is broken or that no other tests cover it. No runtime/build/lint or native dialog/accessibility check ran."
